From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Alder Health POC — evaluation playbook & environment access

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we keep momentum:

Summary of goals
- Validate clinical-note extraction and privacy-safe redaction for downstream analytics
- Measure 95th percentile latency under a realistic burst (100 concurrent sessions)
- Confirm cost-per-1k tokens and expected throughput for production scaling

Success criteria (proposed, attached spreadsheet has details)
- Extraction F1 >= 0.88 on your gold set (we'll run our baseline and share prompts)
- Redaction match >= 98% for PHI categories you care about
- 95th pct latency < 300ms for 512-token responses during dedicated sandbox load tests
- No outbound data leaves your VPC for the VPC option; hosted trial must comply with your retention policy

Environment options (we discussed three):
1) Hosted Redwood demo (fastest): easy to spin up, lowest friction, shared infra; ideal for early model iteration and prompt tuning.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool we provision for Alder): predictable performance, isolated, supports load testing.
3) VPC-connected private trial (your cloud): required if Alder needs all data to remain in your VPC and to use your KMS.

What we need from Alder to finalize the plan
- Quick decision on desired environment: hosted | dedicated sandbox | VPC (Rajiv, you mentioned VPC preference on the call — is that still correct?)
- Access: list of IPs / CIDR for dedicated sandbox egress and a contact for cloud networking if you choose VPC
- Success criteria confirmation and the subset of documents you want us to use as the gold set

Proposed timeline (flexible)
- Week 1 (Nov 9–13): kickoff + access & sample data exchange
- Week 2–3 (Nov 16–27): baseline runs + prompt tuning (hosted/dedicated) or infra onboarding (VPC)
- Week 4 (Nov 30–Dec 4): performance & regression tests, executive readout

Action owners (internal):
- Mina: overall POC lead, baseline runs, and exec readout
- Marissa: infra/setup and dedicated sandbox provisioning
- Ben: security/compliance and SOC2 evidence pack

I attached a draft success_criteria workbook and a lightweight network_access_matrix (CSV) with the fields we typically need.

Next steps: If you can confirm environment preference and share a network contact by Monday (Nov 9), we will lock dates and start provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this underway.

– Mina
Mina Haddad

Thanks Mina — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- VPC is preferred if timeline allows (security team needs to review KMS integration). If VPC will add >2 weeks, we may accept dedicated sandbox for initial prompt/dev work.
- For the gold set, we will share ~200 de-identified notes and a separate locked set for scoring (Rajiv will own).
- Can you confirm whether the dedicated sandbox supports strict egress controls (no external telemetry) and whether you can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and your pen test report?

Rajiv — I'm looping you to confirm the network contact and timeline constraints (we're sensitive to >3-week infra windows).

Mina / Marissa / Ben — please propose minimal networking requirements for the VPC option (CIDR, peering model, and what ports to open).

Emily

Mina / Ben —

Couple quick notes from infra before we commit to dates:

- Dedicated sandbox: we can provision a 1-GPU reserved pool with strict egress rules and host within our tenant. That will meet Alder's egress concerns and give us predictable perf for the 95th pct test. Estimated provisioning lead time: 4 business days after contract/acceptance.
- SOC2 / evidence: Ben, please prepare the standard SOC2 summary + pen test highlight doc and the encryption key management notes. We can share a redacted copy for initial review.
- VPC option: our network team will need an AWS account ID, a list of allowed CIDRs, and an approver for peering. Realistically add ~10 business days for peering + IAM/KMS validation (depends on their cloud team availability).

Recommendation (to present to Emily/Rajiv): 
- Start with dedicated sandbox for initial tuning and latency/load tests. If Alder signs off on the VPC requirements in parallel, we can run a second wave to validate VPC KMS integration. That gives them a faster feedback loop while the longer VPC path proceeds.

I'll draft the provisioning checklist and send to Mina; Mina can forward to Alder.

— Marissa
